reading.title: Bioluminescence in Deep Sea Creatures
reading.passage: Bioluminescence is the production of light by living organisms through chemical reactions. In the deep ocean where sunlight cannot penetrate, many creatures have evolved this remarkable ability. Fish, jellyfish, and other organisms use bioluminescence for various purposes: to attract prey, communicate with potential mates, or confuse predators. Scientists estimate that approximately 90% of deep-sea creatures produce some form of light, making bioluminescence one of the most common biological phenomena in the ocean.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary reason deep-sea creatures evolved bioluminescence?
options: To survive in darkness where sunlight cannot reach
To attract sunlight from the surface
To communicate with surface animals
To create warmth in cold water
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '햇빛이 도달하지 못하는 심해에서 많은 생물들이 이 능력을 진화시켰다'고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a use of bioluminescence?
options: Attracting prey
Communicating with mates
Confusing predators
Producing heat
questions.explanation: 지문에서 생물발광의 사용 목적으로 먹이 유인, 짝짓기 신호, 포식자 혼동만 언급되었으며, 열 생산은 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.q: What does the statistic about 90% of deep-sea creatures suggest?
options: Bioluminescence is a rare adaptation
Bioluminescence is extremely common in the ocean
Most creatures prefer other survival methods
Deep-sea creatures are not well adapted
questions.explanation: 심해 생물의 약 90%가 생물발광을 생산한다는 통계는 이것이 매우 흔한 적응 현상임을 보여줍니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the statement: 'Technology has made human relationships weaker rather than stronger'? Use specific examples to support your position.

structure.intro: Clear thesis statement 제시 (동의 또는 불동의 명확히 표현). 예: 'While technology has some drawbacks, I believe it has ultimately strengthened human relationships.'
structure.body1: 첫 번째 주장: 구체적 예시 포함 (예: 소셜 미디어로 먼 거리의 친구와 연락 유지, 화상통화로 가족 연결). 2-3개 문장.
structure.body2: 두 번째 주장: 반박적 관점 인정하면서도 본인의 입장 강화 (예: 면대면 만남의 중요성 인정하지만, 기술이 이를 보완함). 2-3개 문장.
structure.conclusion: 핵심 아이디어 재강조 및 광범위한 함의 제시. 예: 'In conclusion, technology is a tool that can strengthen or weaken relationships depending on how we use it.'

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to work in a stable job with predictable income. Others prefer to take risks and start their own business. Which do you prefer and why?
useful_expressions: In my opinion, I prefer to...
sample_points: 안정적인 직업: 정기적인 급여, 건강보험 등의 이점이 있어 재정 계획이 용이하고 스트레스가 적음
자신의 사업: 창의성 발휘, 성공 시 높은 소득 가능, 자유도와 성취감이 큼

listening.title: University Library Workshop on Research Methods
listening.script: Professor: Good morning, everyone. I'm Dr. Chen, and today we're discussing effective research strategies for your thesis projects. Many students struggle with finding reliable sources online. The key is to use academic databases like JSTOR and Google Scholar rather than general search engines. These databases filter peer-reviewed articles, which means experts have already verified the information. Additionally, always check the author's credentials and publication date. Outdated information can mislead your research. I also recommend visiting our library's reference desk. Our librarians are experts at helping students find quality sources. Remember, quantity doesn't equal quality. Ten well-researched sources are better than fifty mediocre ones. Does anyone have questions about accessing these databases?

questions.q: What is the main topic of this lecture?
options: How to write a thesis
Strategies for finding reliable research sources
The history of academic databases
How to become a librarian
questions.explanation: 교수는 학생들이 신뢰할 수 있는 자료를 찾기 위한 효과적인 연구 전략, 특히 학술 데이터베이스 사용과 정보 검증 방법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.q: Why does Professor Chen recommend using academic databases instead of general search engines?
options: They are faster and easier to use
They contain more information
They filter peer-reviewed articles verified by experts
They are cheaper than general search engines
questions.explanation: 교수는 'These databases filter peer-reviewed articles, which means experts have already verified the information'라고 명확히 설명했습니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what should students check when evaluating sources?
options: The color and design of the webpage
The author's credentials and publication date
The number of advertisements on the page
The speed of loading
questions.explanation: 교수는 '항상 저자의 자격과 출판 날짜를 확인하라'고 명시적으로 조언했습니다.
